data.title: build01 and fw02: Clarify optional-check semantics under the Stage II all-pass gate
data.body:
## Summary

Two task-level checks describe an operation or artifact as optional, but represent its legitimate absence as a positive-weight `skip`. Since Stage II requires every scored check to pass, these skips block the entire stage.

The scorer explicitly documents that `srb_skip_ok` permits the wording of a skip, not exemption from scoring. This issue therefore concerns consistency between the task contract and the checks, rather than proposing that all skips should be ignored.

The relevant task and scoring code was checked against commit `ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340`. The observations below come from downstream Harbor runs.

## 1. build01: optional macros can independently cause a zero

In [test_macros.py](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake/tests/behavioural/modules/macros/test_macros.py):

- `OPTIONAL` is described as “presence not required.”
- `test_optional_macro_value_when_present` has the `srb_skip_ok` marker.
- An absent macro produces `pytest.skip(... "not defined (permitted)")`.

Observed result:

```text
Audit: pass
Behavioural: 4711 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped
macros module: 151/160, complete=false
Final score: 0
blocked_by: behavioural-incomplete
Stage III: not run
```

All nine skipped checks carry:

```json
{
  "verdict": "skip",
  "weight": 1.0,
  "metadata": {"permitted_skip": true}
}
```

The absent macros are:

```text
LT_OBJDIR
PACKAGE
PACKAGE_BUGREPORT
PACKAGE_NAME
PACKAGE_STRING
PACKAGE_TARNAME
PACKAGE_URL
PACKAGE_VERSION
VERSION
```

These skips are the only behavioural blockers in this run.

However, [instruction §1.4](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake/instruction.md) also requires the same macro set. Could you clarify whether these macros are actually optional, or required for a fully passing submission?

## 2. fw02: a build script is optional, but its absence prevents full credit

The [task instructions](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/fw02-jsonserver-express-to-fastify/instruction.md) allow native ESM without transpilation and describe running a build script conditionally.

The [install runner](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/fw02-jsonserver-express-to-fastify/tests/behavioural/modules/install/run.py) emits:

```text
install/build: skip
the package declares no build script; nothing to build
```

Observed install result:

```text
5 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped
complete=false
```

Consequently, a submission without a build script cannot satisfy the Stage II all-pass gate, even if installation, packaging, startup and behaviour are otherwise correct.

Our observed fw02 submission also failed an Audit gate and other behavioural checks. We are **not** attributing its entire zero score to this skip; it exposes an additional contract inconsistency.

## Suggested resolution

Please clarify the intended task-level semantics:

- If absence is allowed, represent legitimate absence as satisfying that check, while preserving failures for an incorrect macro value or a declared build script that fails.
- If presence is required, make the instructions and test wording explicit.

We do not suggest globally excluding skips from scoring, since that could hide missing artifacts or incomplete execution.

## Suggested regression coverage

| Case | Expected distinction |
|---|---|
| build01: optional macro absent | Resolve according to the clarified contract |
| build01: macro present with incorrect value | Fail |
| fw02: native ESM without a build script | No penalty solely for the missing optional step |
| fw02: declared build script fails | Fail |
| Missing required artifact / unexpected skip | Remain a blocker |

data.title: build02: Export-Package byte comparison contradicts the order-insensitive contract
data.body:
## Summary

The build02 instructions specify an order-insensitive, clause-based comparison for `Export-Package` and `Import-Package`. However, `test_required_header_exact` compares the header strings directly.

In a downstream Harbor run, the only behavioural failure was an `Export-Package` value with the same packages and parameter values, but a different order of parameters within one clause.

The relevant instructions and test code were checked against commit `ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340`.

## Declared contract versus implementation

[Instruction §1.6](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build02-gson-maven-to-gradle/instruction.md#L173) says:

> `Export-Package` and `Import-Package` are compared clause by clause, so ordering and whitespace do not matter

The following text identifies packages, versions, `uses:=` sets and `resolution:=optional` as the meaningful content.

But [test_required_header_exact](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build02-gson-maven-to-gradle/tests/behavioural/modules/manifest/test_manifest.py#L109) uses:

```python
assert got == want
```

## Observed result

```text
Audit: pass
Behavioural: 2668 passed, 1 failed
Failed check: manifest/...::test_required_header_exact[Export-Package]
Final score: 0
Stage III: not run
```

The complete values in the failure are:

```text
State A:
com.google.gson;uses:="com.google.gson.reflect,com.google.gson.stream";version="2.10.1",com.google.gson.annotations;version="2.10.1",com.google.gson.reflect;version="2.10.1",com.google.gson.stream;version="2.10.1"

Produced:
com.google.gson;version="2.10.1";uses:="com.google.gson.reflect,com.google.gson.stream",com.google.gson.annotations;version="2.10.1",com.google.gson.reflect;version="2.10.1",com.google.gson.stream;version="2.10.1"
```

Only the order of `uses:=` and `version=` in the first clause differs. The package list, versions and `uses:=` values are unchanged.

## Minimal reproduction of the difference

This Python snippet compares the observed values without splitting commas inside quoted parameter values. It illustrates the observed mismatch; it is not intended as a complete production OSGi parser.

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
def split_quoted(value, separator):
    parts, start, quoted, escaped = [], 0, False, False
    for i, ch in enumerate(value):
        if escaped:
            escaped = False
        elif ch == "\\" and quoted:
            escaped = True
        elif ch == '"':
            quoted = not quoted
        elif ch == separator and not quoted:
            parts.append(value[start:i].strip())
            start = i + 1
    assert not quoted
    return parts + [value[start:].strip()]

def canonical(value):
    clauses = [split_quoted(clause, ";") for clause in split_quoted(value, ",")]
    return sorted((clause[0], sorted(clause[1:])) for clause in clauses)

suffix = (
    ',com.google.gson.annotations;version="2.10.1"'
    ',com.google.gson.reflect;version="2.10.1"'
    ',com.google.gson.stream;version="2.10.1"'
)
expected = (
    'com.google.gson;uses:="com.google.gson.reflect,com.google.gson.stream"'
    ';version="2.10.1"' + suffix
)
produced = (
    'com.google.gson;version="2.10.1"'
    ';uses:="com.google.gson.reflect,com.google.gson.stream"' + suffix
)

assert produced != expected
assert canonical(produced) == canonical(expected)
print("Raw strings differ; parsed clauses and parameters match")
PY
```

## Expected behavior

The two values should compare equal under the task's documented contract. Changes to package membership, versions, `uses:=` sets or resolution directives must remain failures.

This issue does not propose relaxing unrelated headers whose exact contents are part of the contract.

## Suggested fix and regression coverage

Use a quote-aware structural comparison for `Export-Package` and `Import-Package`, preserving the distinction between attributes (`=`) and directives (`:=`). Avoid a plain `split(",")`, because the observed `uses:=` value itself contains a comma.

Suggested cases:

| Change | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Only clause/parameter ordering or insignificant whitespace | Pass |
| Package added or removed | Fail |
| Export version changed | Fail |
| `uses:=` membership changed | Fail |
| `resolution:=optional` changed or removed | Fail |
| A header requiring exact equality changes | Continue to fail |

## Impact and validation boundary

This single failure blocked the entire Stage II despite the other 2668 behavioural checks passing. The mismatch is verified from the emitted values and the published task contract; it is not inferred from an aggregate score.

Stage III did not run. Fixing this comparison would allow the submission to be evaluated further, but does not establish a final passing score or justify automatically assigning full credit.

data.title: lang04: Truncated cargo metadata JSON breaks cross-module structural checks
data.body:
## Summary

The lang04 harness transports `cargo metadata` output between modules through a human-readable log summary that truncates long stdout. A later module treats that truncated string as JSON, catches the parse error and returns an empty object.

Consequently, a successful `cargo metadata` command can be reported as having failed to run or parse, causing the workspace-members and crate-versions checks to fail.

The relevant task code was checked against commit `ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340`. The data-loss mechanism is reproduced below with synthetic valid JSON. Attribution to the observed run is strongly supported by its logs, but the original full cargo stdout was not available in the collected artifacts.

## Code path

1. [Builder.metadata](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/lang04-acorn-js-to-rust/tests/behavioural/lib/build.py#L410) captures the command result.
2. [BuildOutcome.summary](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/lang04-acorn-js-to-rust/tests/behavioural/lib/build.py#L119) serializes the metadata result using `result.brief()`.
3. [Result.brief](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/lang04-acorn-js-to-rust/tests/behavioural/lib/vlib.py#L60) defaults to a 4000-character limit, replacing the middle of long stdout with an elision marker.
4. [BuildOutcome.from_summary](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/lang04-acorn-js-to-rust/tests/behavioural/lib/build.py#L129) reconstructs the metadata with `Result.from_brief`.
5. [IntegrityAuditor.metadata](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/lang04-acorn-js-to-rust/tests/behavioural/lib/audit.py#L368) calls `json.loads` on the reconstructed stdout. On `ValueError`, it keeps an empty dictionary.

```text
valid cargo JSON
  → Result.brief(): head + elision marker + tail
  → Result.from_brief(): command still has returncode=0 / ok=true
  → json.loads(): invalid JSON
  → auditor metadata becomes {}
```

The summary is suitable for a log, but is lossy transport for machine-readable data.

## Observed run

A downstream Harbor run reported:

```text
Audit: pass
Behavioural: 16036 passed, 3 failed

Structural failures:
  struct/workspace-members: cargo metadata did not run or did not parse
  struct/crate-versions: cargo metadata did not run; cannot read versions
```

The build log records `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps --offline ...` succeeding before the separate structural module reports these failures. Build and installation also succeeded.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from a repository checkout at the commit above, using Python 3.10+. This imports only the task's standard-library `vlib` helper and does not invoke Cargo, build a submission, start a container or call a model.

**The payload is synthetic, not the original stdout from the observed run.**

```bash
python3 -B - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

lib = Path("tasks/lang04-acorn-js-to-rust/tests/behavioural/lib").resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(lib))
from vlib import Result

document = {
    "packages": [{
        "name": "acorn",
        "version": "8.14.0",
        "description": "x" * 5000,
    }]
}
raw = json.dumps(document).encode("utf-8")
original = Result(
    argv=["cargo", "metadata"],
    cwd="/synthetic",
    returncode=0,
    stdout=raw,
    stderr=b"",
    duration=0.1,
)

assert json.loads(original.stdout) == document
restored = Result.from_brief(original.brief())
assert original.ok and restored.ok

print("original bytes:", len(original.stdout))
print("restored bytes:", len(restored.stdout))
print("command still reports success:", restored.ok)
try:
    json.loads(restored.stdout)
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    print("restored stdout is not valid JSON")
else:
    raise AssertionError("Expected the current brief() path to truncate the JSON")
PY
```

Observed output:

```text
original bytes: 5073
restored bytes: 4027
command still reports success: True
restored stdout is not valid JSON
```

The current auditor catches this parse error and returns `{}`, producing the same class of structural diagnostic seen in the run.

## Expected behavior

A successful, valid metadata document should survive the module boundary without alteration. Structural checks should inspect its package/workspace information rather than a truncated log representation.

## Suggested fix

- Preserve full machine-readable metadata separately, for example as parsed JSON or a dedicated file referenced by the build ledger.
- Keep `brief()` for human-readable logs; simply reconstructing a `Result` from it cannot recover the original data.
- Check the earlier command-capture boundary too: `vlib.run` has a default output cap, while `Builder.metadata` currently does not request full capture. Preventing only the later 4000-character truncation would leave the earlier limit in place.
- Report an actual parse error distinctly from command failure, so it does not become an unexplained empty metadata object.

## Suggested regression coverage

| Case | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Valid metadata below the summary limit | Parses after transport |
| Valid metadata above 4000 characters | Parses after transport |
| Valid metadata above the command-capture limit | Preserved through the designated machine-data path |
| Command returns malformed JSON | Clear parse diagnostic |
| Command fails | Clear command-failure diagnostic |

data.title: build01: SSP switch detection can select NOEXECSTACK capability variables
data.body:
## Summary

`test_ssp_can_be_turned_off` can select a CMake capability-probe variable for non-executable stacks instead of the submission's actual stack-protector option. It then tests the unrelated variable and reports that SSP cannot be disabled.

The relevant task code was checked against commit `ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340`. The observed failure comes from a downstream Harbor run; the selector reproducer below uses the upstream source directly and needs no candidate build or model call.

## Observed result

```text
Audit: pass
Behavioural: 4719 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped
Failed check: hardening/...::test_ssp_can_be_turned_off
Final score: 0
Stage III: not run
```

The failure reports that `SODIUM_ACCEPTS_NOEXECSTACK=OFF` still leaves 117 translation units compiled with `-fstack-protector`.

The submission actually declares:

```cmake
option(SODIUM_USE_SSP "Use stack-smashing protection when supported" ON)
```

Its compile-flag logic guards `-fstack-protector` with `SODIUM_USE_SSP` and the corresponding compiler/linker capability checks. Separately, `SODIUM_ACCEPTS_NOEXECSTACK` controls `-Wl,-z,noexecstack`.

The reported test therefore does not exercise the submission's SSP control.

## Code path

- [Instruction §1.10](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake/instruction.md#L174) requires SSP to remain overridable, without prescribing a CMake option name.
- [test_hardening.py](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake/tests/behavioural/modules/hardening/test_hardening.py#L572) asks `feature_switch(r"SSP", r"STACK")` for a control.
- [Build.feature_switch](https://github.com/Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench/blob/ecbb6925ebdc7259cde4a709187dc58beca76340/tasks/build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake/tests/behavioural/lib/builder.py#L1059) sorts all cache keys, then returns the first key matching any pattern.

`SODIUM_ACCEPTS_NOEXECSTACK` sorts before `SODIUM_USE_SSP` and matches the broad `STACK` pattern. Pattern order does not give `SSP` matches priority, because the outer loop iterates over names.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from a repository checkout at the commit above, using Python 3.10+:

```bash
python3 -B - <<'PY'
import ast
from pathlib import Path
import re
from types import SimpleNamespace

path = Path(
    "tasks/build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake/"
    "tests/behavioural/lib/builder.py"
)
tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
method = next(
    node for node in ast.walk(tree)
    if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "feature_switch"
)
scope = {"re": re}
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[method], type_ignores=[]), str(path), "exec"), scope)

cache = {
    "SODIUM_ACCEPTS_NOEXECSTACK": "1",
    "SODIUM_ACCEPTS_STACK_PROTECTOR_COMPILE": "1",
    "SODIUM_ACCEPTS_STACK_PROTECTOR_LINK": "1",
    "SODIUM_USE_SSP": "ON",
}
build = SimpleNamespace(is_cmake=True, cmake_cache=lambda: cache)
selected = scope["feature_switch"](build, r"SSP", r"STACK")
print(selected)
assert selected == ("SODIUM_ACCEPTS_NOEXECSTACK", "OFF")
PY
```

Actual output:

```text
('SODIUM_ACCEPTS_NOEXECSTACK', 'OFF')
```

This isolates the upstream selection logic with representative cache entries. It does not configure or execute the submission.

## Expected behavior

The test should exercise an actual SSP/stack-protector control. An unrelated `NOEXECSTACK` capability variable must not be selected merely because its name contains `STACK`.

If a control cannot be identified reliably, the diagnostic should distinguish that from having tested the control and found it ineffective.

## Suggested fix and regression coverage

Please consider distinguishing user-facing feature options from internal capability probes, and using SSP-specific matching rather than unrestricted `STACK` matching. The fix should not hardcode this submission's option name.

Useful regression cases:

- An SSP option coexists with a lexicographically earlier `NOEXECSTACK` probe.
- Internal `STACK_PROTECTOR` capability variables coexist with the actual feature option.
- The selected option genuinely fails to disable SSP: the test must still fail.
- No identifiable SSP option exists: retain an explicit, policy-consistent diagnostic.

## Impact and validation boundary

This was the run's only failed behavioural check, so it independently blocked Stage II and prevented Stage III from running.

The incorrect selection is reproduced, and the candidate source contains the intended control. We have **not** rebuilt the candidate with `SODIUM_USE_SSP=OFF`; a corrected check still needs to establish that the control works. This issue does not request an automatic passing score or full credit for the submission.

data.title: Stage II: State A does not pass its own behavioural suite on 4 tasks (build01, fw01, fw02, fw05)
data.body:
Hello, thanks for releasing SWE Refactor Bench!  

We ran each task's Stage II with **State A itself as the submission** — the tree unpacked from
`environment/original.tar.gz` — on the assumption that the recorded expectations were derived from
State A, so it should pass every check by construction.

Method, so this is reproducible:

- benchmark at `f8ba808` (tip of main at the time of writing)
- behavioural images built from that checkout's `tests/behavioural` contexts
- driven through the repo's own `swerefactor.ladder.run_stage()` for the `behavioural` stage only,
  with `--repo` and `--original` both pointing at the unpacked State A tree
- `--network none` (the stage's own setting), no model calls involved

Stage I legitimately fails in this configuration (State A has not migrated), which does not matter
here: Stage II runs regardless and reports its measurement.

## Result

| task | State A: failing checks | total checks | modules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **fw05**-miniserve-actix-to-axum | **269** | 12,466 | `listing` 249, `archives` 20 |
| **fw01**-httpbin-flask-to-asgi | **15** | 2,832 | `corpus` 15 |
| **build01**-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake | **6** | 4,720 | `cmake-package` 5, `pkgconfig` 1 |
| **fw02**-jsonserver-express-to-fastify | **6** | 6,760 | `read` 3, `options` 3 |

The other 16 tasks are clean. Thirteen have zero failing checks. **pf02** has exactly one: **platform/.../test_render_sync_refuses_a_platform_without_sync**, which asserts that **renderSync()** throws on a platform whose **sync** flag is false — a property that only exists once the port introduces the platform abstraction, so State A returning CSS there is correct behaviour for State A, and our own submission passes that check. **lang02** and **lang06** are excluded from this method entirely.



Because Stage II is all-or-nothing for its 40 points, a single unwinnable check caps the task at 0
for **every** submission. On these four tasks, no submission built from the current release can
score above 0.

## One mechanism, pinned to the byte (fw01)

`tests/behavioural/lib/harness/corpus.py` builds the multipart bodies itself:

```python
_MP_BOUNDARY = "----SWERefactorBoundary7MA4YWxkTrZu0gW"

def _multipart(parts):
    out = []
    for name, filename, value in parts:
        out.append(f"--{_MP_BOUNDARY}\r\n")
        ...
```

Executing the shipped function and comparing with the shipped recording:

| case | `_multipart()` today | `data/responses.json` recorded `Content-Length` |
|---|---|---|
| `mp-single-field` | **133** | **129** |
| `mp-two-fields` | **222** | **216** |
| `mp-repeated-field` | — | 216 |

The delta is exactly `2 × (parts + 1)`, i.e. two bytes per boundary delimiter line. The recording was
made by a version of `_multipart()` that terminated boundary lines with `\n`; the shipped one uses
`\r\n`. The three failing checks are `corpus/.../test_body[mp-single-field]`,
`[mp-two-fields]`, `[mp-repeated-field]`, plus twelve more multipart cases, and the failure reads
`body mismatch (515B vs 515B)` — same length, different content — because httpbin echoes the
`Content-Length` header it received.

Reproducer, no container needed:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
src = open('tasks/fw01-httpbin-flask-to-asgi/tests/behavioural/lib/harness/corpus.py').read()
seg = src[src.index('_MP_BOUNDARY ='):src.index('_MP_CT =')]
ns = {}; exec(seg, ns)
print(len(ns['_multipart']([("a", None, "1")]).encode()))   # -> 133
PY
grep -o '"Content-Length": "[0-9]*"' \
  tasks/fw01-httpbin-flask-to-asgi/tests/behavioural/data/responses.json | sort -u | head
```

We did not pin the mechanism for the other three. Their expectations are runtime products
(a libsodium consumer's printed probe value for build01, directory-listing bodies carrying file
sizes and mtimes for fw05, static index bodies for fw02), so we cannot compute them statically the
way fw01 allows. The failing check ids are listed at the end.

## What we ruled out

- **Not our images being stale.** We verified for each task that the behavioural image was built
  from a context identical to the checkout under test (`git diff --name-only <image commit> f8ba808
  -- tasks/<task>/tests/behavioural/`). One task, fw06, did have a stale image on our side — its
  earlier failures disappeared entirely (485/485) once we rebuilt from `f8ba808`, so fw06 is *not*
  in the table above.
- **Not dependency drift.** For fw01, `httpx` is hash-pinned to `0.28.1`, matching the
  `python-httpx/0.28.1` User-Agent echoed inside the recording itself.
- **Not lang02 / lang06.** State A fails almost everything there, but for a different reason: those
  suites drive the *target platform's* artifact (`not run: the submission produced no runnable
  program`, `the shared configuration installed no usable jar`), so State A is not a runnable
  submission and this method has no judgement power on them. Independently, our own runs show those
  checks are winnable — across our runs, 2,604 of lang06's 2,608 checks were passed by at least one
  submission, and lang02's never-passed checks are invariant assertions
  ("compress then decompress must return the input") that a correct implementation satisfies by
  construction. We are not reporting those two.

## Suggestion

The repository already contains the pattern that prevents this. In `lang01`–`lang07` and `pf03`,
`tests/behavioural/lib/freeze.py` runs **at image build time**: it builds the reference from State A,
generates the corpus, and records every expectation into an immutable digested blob. Quoting
`tasks/lang02-zlib-c-to-java/tests/behavioural/Dockerfile`:

> freeze.py runs here, at build time. … By the time a submission exists the answers are already
> fixed and digested; grading only compares against them.

All eight tasks that use it are clean. All four tasks in the table above are among the twelve that
ship a static recording instead. Two of those twelve (`fw02`, `fw05`) do ship the recorder
(`lib/harness/capture.py`) — `fw02` even guards it, refusing to grade when `exchanges.py` is edited
without re-recording — while `fw01` and `build01` ship no generator for their `data/*.json` at all.

Concretely, in decreasing order of how much it would help:

1. Regenerate the four recordings (or extend `freeze.py`-style build-time capture to them).
2. Add the fw02-style provenance guard to every task that keeps a static recording, so that editing
   the code which produces the requests fails the build instead of silently invalidating the golden.
3. Consider adding this check to CI: grading State A against its own Stage II is offline, needs no
   model calls, and took us under an hour for all 20 tasks.

We are happy to send PRs regenerating `fw02` and `fw05` with the shipped `capture.py` if that is
useful. For `fw01` and `build01` we would be guessing at the original procedure, so those seem
better done by you.

## Appendix: failing check ids

<details><summary>build01 (6)</summary>

```
cmake-package/.../test_cmake_package.py::test_shared_consumer_runs_and_matches_state_a
cmake-package/.../test_cmake_package.py::test_static_consumer_runs_and_matches_state_a
cmake-package/.../test_cmake_package.py::test_shared_only_consumer_builds
cmake-package/.../test_cmake_package.py::test_static_only_consumer_builds
cmake-package/.../test_cmake_package.py::test_minimal_install_is_consumable
```

`build01-libsodium-autotools-to-cmake`.

Our submission passed Stage I and passed 4,714/4,720 Stage II checks. All six
failures came from the same consumer-output mismatch:

```text
Our submission: 1.0.20|26|2|32|ff67
Frozen golden:  1.0.20|26|2|32|dbcb
```

To verify this independently of our submission, we rebuilt the published
State A `original.tar.gz` inside the published
`swerefactor/build01-behavioural:1` image and ran the exact `CONSUMER_C`
program used by the Stage II suite.

The reproduced State A output was:

```text
1.0.20|26|2|32|ff67
```

Relevant published artifacts:

```text
Benchmark commit:
1270471ccb5e6f254627784658d4e29acb90b953

Behavioural image:
sha256:5eca88609017bdc4b8e8935e17802ae71b97eb210fae6e57d8d220e3c7b8fad8

original.tar.gz:
sha256:cf7b6ea531362d7855e6625a8bc71e42f3b9712ea5f2436c9775642c3cd2315e
```

The public official GPT-5.6 Sol max run reports 100% Stage II checks and a

data.title: # [Bug] `fw06-behavioural` image cannot be built because the corpus and golden recording disagree
data.body:
# [Bug] `fw06-behavioural` image cannot be built because the corpus and golden recording disagree

Hi, thanks for releasing SWE Refactor Bench!

The Stage 2 image for `fw06-uploadserver-gorillamux-to-nethttp` fails a deterministic build-time self-check because the committed request corpus and the committed State A golden recording have different fingerprints.

The corpus and recording both contain the same 87 case IDs, so this does not appear to be a missing-record problem. Instead, at least one fingerprinted request input or profile flag differs from the corpus against which `golden-statea.json` was captured.

## Environment

- Repository: `Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench`
- Reproduced at commit: `4e2109211d0952915168a0ae7d5745def6ff0913`
- Platform: Linux `x86_64`
- Docker client: `20.10.18`
- Docker server: `28.0.4`

The affected files are:

```text
tasks/fw06-uploadserver-gorillamux-to-nethttp/tests/behavioural/
├── Dockerfile
├── data/golden-statea.json
└── lib/harness/corpus.py
```

## Minimal reproduction (no Docker required)

Run this command from the repository root:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import sys

root = "tasks/fw06-uploadserver-gorillamux-to-nethttp/tests/behavioural"
sys.path.insert(0, f"{root}/lib")

from harness import corpus

with open(f"{root}/data/golden-statea.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    recording = json.load(f)

cases = corpus.all_cases()
case_ids = {case["id"] for case in cases}
record_ids = set(recording["records"])

print(f"corpus cases:         {len(cases)}")
print(f"recording records:    {len(recording['records'])}")
print(f"same case IDs:        {case_ids == record_ids}")
print(f"missing records:      {sorted(case_ids - record_ids)}")
print(f"orphan records:       {sorted(record_ids - case_ids)}")
print(f"current fingerprint:  {corpus.fingerprint()}")
print(f"recorded fingerprint: {recording['corpus_fingerprint']}")
PY
```

Actual output:

```text
corpus cases:         87
recording records:    87
same case IDs:        True
missing records:      []
orphan records:       []
current fingerprint:  67dfd21e7c88cf990d89bbb78109b5787c0d772b95206bac82efe940551672aa
recorded fingerprint: 2c2e73398e2c5d2b604ee8bf06ebc7501f0b33a2138936f8023db70cc80e925d
```

The fingerprint covers the profile flag lists and every request's ID, profile, suite, method, target, headers, body digest, and mutation flag. Therefore, equal counts and equal IDs do not establish that the recording answers the requests currently defined by the corpus.

## Image-build reproduction

From the repository root:

```bash
docker build -t swerefactor/infra:1 infra

docker build \
  -t swerefactor/fw06-behavioural:1 \
  tasks/fw06-uploadserver-gorillamux-to-nethttp/tests/behavioural
```

The build reaches the self-check in `tests/behavioural/Dockerfile` and fails with:

```text
corpus    : 87 cases over 4 profiles, fingerprint 67dfd21e7c88cf990d89bbb78109b5787c0d772b95206bac82efe940551672aa
recording : 87 records, captured against 2c2e73398e2c5d2b604ee8bf06ebc7501f0b33a2138936f8023db70cc80e925d
FATAL: the suite and its recording disagree:
  the recording answers corpus 2c2e73398e2c5d2b604ee8bf06ebc7501f0b33a2138936f8023db70cc80e925d, this corpus is 67dfd21e7c88cf990d89bbb78109b5787c0d772b95206bac82efe940551672aa
```

## Impact

The committed image `swerefactor/fw06-behavioural:1` cannot be built. Consequently, the official evaluation ladder cannot perform Stage 2 for `fw06`.

This should not be treated as a submission failure. If the missing Stage 2 image is allowed to flow into scoring as an ordinary failure, `fw06` can receive a misleading zero and Stage 3 will not run, even though the failure is in the benchmark artifact rather than in the submitted migration.

## Why bypassing the check would not be safe

The Dockerfile check appears to be working as intended. Replacing only the fingerprint stored in `golden-statea.json`, or removing the assertion, could pair responses captured from old requests with different current requests.

For example, `corpus.py` explicitly explains that changing a target from `/files/sub%2Fb.txt` to `/files/sub/b.txt` can preserve counts and IDs while changing the router behavior being measured. In that situation, replaying the old response could silently grade the wrong contract.

## Expected behavior

The committed corpus should match the corpus used to capture `data/golden-statea.json`, and the Stage 2 image should build successfully from a clean checkout.

Could you please confirm which artifact is authoritative?

1. If the published results were graded with the existing golden recording, could the request/profile spellings used for that capture be restored in `lib/harness/corpus.py`?
2. If the current corpus is authoritative, could `golden-statea.json` be reviewed and recaptured from the frozen State A implementation?

The public history for the `fw06` behavioural directory appears to begin with the release commit, so I could not identify an earlier public version of `corpus.py` whose fingerprint is `2c2e7339...`.

## Suggested regression check

Whichever artifact is corrected, the following should hold before the image is published:

```python
assert set(recording["records"]) == {case["id"] for case in corpus.all_cases()}
assert recording["corpus_fingerprint"] == corpus.fingerprint()
```

The second assertion should be satisfied by restoring the exact recorded requests or by producing a reviewed new capture, rather than by editing the fingerprint field alone.

data.title: Where can I download the full evaluation trajectories (333 MB JSONL)?
data.body:
Hi, thanks for releasing SWE Refactor Bench!

The project page states under "What we release": "Trajectories — 248k calls. Every tool call of every graded run, in full, across two harnesses", and the Runs page header mentions "Trajectories 333 MB JSONL, one file per run".

However, I couldn't find any way to actually download them:
- The Runs table has no links to per-run trajectory files or log pages (the last column only shows a tool-sequence shape thumbnail).
- This repo contains the harness, task definitions and docs, but no trajectories/results directory and no GitHub Release.
- There's no related dataset on HuggingFace either.
- The only downloadable file I found is https://lab.einsia.ai/swe-refactor-bench/data/runs.json, which contains per-run telemetry summaries (message/tool-call counts, token usage, duration) but not the conversations themselves.

Could you share where the full trajectories are hosted, or whether/when they will be released? Thanks!

data.title: [Bug] Three stage images fail to build on main@1270471
data.body:
Hi, thanks for releasing SWE Refactor Bench!  
I encountered a failure while building the image for SWE-Refactor-bench; the details are as follows:


## Environment

- Repository: `Einsia/SWE-Refactor-Bench`
- Commit: `1270471ccb5e6f254627784658d4e29acb90b953`
- Platform: Linux `amd64`, Docker 24.0.9

`PYTHONPATH=infra python3 -m swerefactor validate --task-dir ...` passes all three tasks, but their stage images fail deterministic build-time self-checks. As a result, evaluation cannot start through the official build/run workflow.

## 1. `build02-verification`: offline inputs and digest constants disagree

The verification image fails immediately:

```text
FATAL: /opt/srb/deps.txt has digest 06b23fdbdc3e9821, expected 8c21fb43b03e006d.
```

Its `deps.txt` is missing:

```text
org.sonatype.sisu:sisu-guice:3.2.3:jar:no_aop
```

The environment and behavioural copies already agree. The verification copy and Dockerfile prefixes should be synchronized to:

```text
deps.txt:           1fe5a5321f4b4264
settings.xml:       c649f180bd8671cf
srb-offline.gradle: 3ffe9bd34097ec28
```

I tested this patch with a complete Dockerfile build; all offline Maven and Gradle checks passed.

## 2. `fw04-behavioural`: pytest collection count mismatch

The committed suite collects successfully, but collects `11397` tests while the Dockerfile requires `11510`:

```text
collection_rc=0 collected=11397 expected=11510
```

The preceding corpus checks pass: both fingerprints match the recording, and all 728 declared corpus cases are present.

If `11397` is the intended suite total, both occurrences of `11510` should be updated. Until then, the behavioural image cannot be built and evaluation cannot start.

## 3. `fw05-behavioural`: golden capture and corpus disagree

The committed self-check fails:

```text
RuntimeError: responses.json.gz was captured against a different corpus
(92bdd49e7c73eb06 != 4ce68aeb270d99b2).
```

The golden capture contains inputs such as `X-Rmb-*`, `application/x-rmb`, and `RMB <fw05>`, while the current corpus uses `X-Srb-*`, `application/x-srb`, and `SRB <fw05>`.

This requires either restoring the corpus used for the capture or reviewing and committing a fresh capture. Merely replacing the fingerprint would risk pairing recorded responses with different requests.

## Expected behavior

All committed stage images should build successfully from a clean checkout using the official workflow. Currently, these three build failures prevent their evaluations from starting.
